span.term: Learning-driven loss of SOM-IN boutons reduces inhibition of distal dendrites, which depolarizes those dendrites and creates conditions favouring synaptic potentiation and the stabilization of new spines

span.label: the same variable is pushed in both directions and produces the same behavioural deficit, which is evidence for an optimum rather than for a direction of effect

span.label: the spatial logic is read off the anatomy: the compartment that changes is exactly the one the decreasing interneuron type targets, and the compartment that does not change is the one the increasing type targets

span.label: a confound is named and then measured directly rather than argued away - fewer SOM boutons need not mean less inhibition onto excitatory dendrites, so the inhibitory synapses themselves are imaged
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the specificity of the manipulation is established twice over: the same stimulation after learning does nothing, and the same protocol on a different interneuron type does nothing
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: imaging three times a day separates the clocks of the two elements, showing the inhibitory change leads the excitatory one
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: an untrained-but-water-restricted control and an anatomically adjacent cortical area both serve as internal controls for the imaging itself

span.label: retraining a month later shows no further reorganization, which localises the whole phenomenon to initial acquisition

span.label: the optogenetic controls rule out the two trivial explanations separately - expression without light, and light without training

span.label: sparse labelling by dilute Cre virus is what makes individual spines resolvable across eleven daily sessions

span.label: the mechanism proposed is left explicitly as a postulate, tied to prior work on dendritic excitability rather than measured here
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the opposite change in the other interneuron type is offered as speculation and labelled as such

span.label: The authors cannot rule out that circuit components other than SOM-INs also affect spine dynamics and learning.
span.note: what this limits: the sufficiency claim about SOM-INs: WE CANNOT CLAIM THAT SOM-INs ARE THE ONLY CIRCUIT COMPONENT WHOSE MANIPULATION AFFECTS SPINE DYNAMICS AND LEARNING

span.label: The scoring-correction rule may cause the reported spine/bouton dynamics to be underestimated.

span.label: the homeostatic interpretation of the PV increase is explicitly speculative

Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Motor learning reorganized dendritic spines only on the distal apical dendrites of L2/3 excitatory neurons in layer 1, leaving perisomatic dendrites stable, i.e. the plasticity was confined to a specific dendritic compartment.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The two inhibitory neuron subtypes changed in opposite directions during training: SOM-IN boutons dropped early while PV-IN boutons rose gradually.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Both increasing and decreasing SOM-IN activity optogenetically disrupted spine dynamics and impaired the acquisition of stereotyped movements, so learning depends on an intermediate level of SOM inhibition.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Inhibitory postsynaptic sites on the distal dendrites of excitatory neurons, imaged as Gephyrin-GFP puncta, also declined during learning, confirming that the SOM bouton loss translates into less dendritic inhibition of excitatory cells.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Activating SOM-INs did not block the formation of new spines but blocked their stabilization and additionally destabilized older spines.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Silencing SOM-INs left spine formation intact while nearly eliminating spine loss, showing spine turnover is bidirectionally sensitive to SOM inhibition.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The bouton changes were specific to trained forelimb cortex: untrained animals and the hindlimb area showed no change.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Behaviourally, SOM-IN activation increased missed trials and prevented movement kinematics from becoming stereotyped.
